newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares edge higher in late trade with dlr.
newsitem.headline: German shares edge higher in late trade with dlr.

text.p: German shares moved into positive territory in late Friday trade as the dollar firmed above the 1.50 mark level, with traders and analysts saying that the DAX index could again test the 2,800 level next week.
The IBIS DAX index of all-day electronic trade stood 1.31 points higher at 2,766.60 by 1508 GMT, off the low of 2,750 touched earlier in the day after a period of consolidation.

Assuming that Wall Street's current general trend upwards is continued next week, dealers said the German market could go on to break through the record 2,800 level that the main DAX approached but fell short of last week.
Analysts said the environment was now right for selective purchases of stocks.
"The current consolidation should now allow investors to build up positions in high-value companies with solid financial structures and good product portfolios," one analyst said.
Chemicals and drugs group BASF AG, up 30 pfennigs at 52.65 marks, and industrial concern Daimler-Benz AG, up 36 pfennigs at 97.31, were cited as favourites by a number of banks.
December DAX futures meanwhile traded at 2,769.0, 0.5 points lower, but up from a day's low of 2,755.

In an investment note, the Vereins- und Westbank said that any further rises in the cash market would now have to be based on higher corporate earnings following the publication of the latest Ifo business confidence index earlier this week.

The bank said that the index, which was better than some had expected, had removed any lingering hopes of a rate cut in the German debt market and with it the "rate-induced gains in the share market".
Deutsche Telekom, the market's latest addition, was generally seen holding a steady course during next week.
Telekom shares, trading 33 pfennigs up at 32.21 in late IBIS, were seen moving between a range of 31 and 33 marks next week.
